state_vocabularies.vocabulary_name: Six server-side checks run on every action, in this order, each a hard stop

business_rules.statement: Every screen belongs to exactly one surface and is reachable from a named navigation entry point on that surface.
Every screen renders all thirteen states of the platform state contract in Section 25.1, either at the contract default or at a stated departure.
Every action on every screen carries an explicit permission status per role from the closed set. No blank cells.

No screen offers an action that its surface is forbidden to perform. The four Command Center exclusions and the on-device prohibition on worker-facing pace are enforced by the absence of the capability in the service, not by the absence of a button.
Every screen has an audit or history route where it touches an audited record, and states plainly where it does not.
Every screen renders in English and Spanish from versioned locale files, with nothing machine-translated at runtime.
Hiding a user-interface control is not security. The authority decision is made on the server, on every call, against the caller's identity, roles, scopes, tenant, and the object's own state.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Server-side check on every endpoint call

business_rules.statement: A screen specification is accepted only when a direct call to the endpoint by a role that must not have it is refused by the server; hidden control is not enforcement.
Loading never renders a zero — a count that has not arrived is shown as a placeholder, not as '0'.
An action the role could never hold is not rendered at all; an action the role could hold in another scope is rendered disabled with the reason.
Under STATE-06 the cause is always named — tenant hard suspension, an archived object, a role without write authority, or a support session; 'read-only' alone is never shown.
Only the Frontline Worker Application has a true offline state. The three web surfaces render a connection-lost banner and enter STATE-08 or STATE-13, because they have no offline mode.
business_rules.applies_to: DOH, Studio, Command Center, Super Admin console

business_rules.statement: Stale content is never presented as current, and the marker is selectable to list what is behind the number.
An accepted action that has not yet taken effect is shown in its true command state and never as done.
Where the failure is an audit-write failure, the screen states that the action did not happen.
If a capability is out of scope, no endpoint exists for it; if it is in scope for another role, the endpoint exists and refuses this caller.
There is no path from a failed fetch to a rendered zero: failure and emptiness are different exits; and no path from an accepted action to a 'done' rendering without the audit commit.
Where a service cannot distinguish 'none exist' from 'query timed out', the screen renders STATE-12 — the more conservative of the two — with 'The platform could not confirm this list'.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Terminal safe state for state collapse

business_rules.statement: Every mutating screen on the Delivery Operations Hub writes its audit event in the same transaction as the change; an action that cannot be audited does not happen.

Under soft suspension master-data screens block writes while operational screens keep working; under hard suspension everything is read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline; under compliance suspension nobody gets in at all.
Every configuration screen validates against the tenant-configuration registry and refuses an out-of-bound value at entry with the bound stated.
The audit log records identity and action, never an 'acting as role' fiction; the permission matrix is per role but the record is per person.

The Reviewer must be a different person from the Author and no role performs two stages on one submission; the Release Authority cannot be bypassed; the locale completeness check blocks publication in an incomplete locale.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Server-side governance check in the Studio

business_rules.statement: Authoring is web-only and requires a connection, so there is no offline state on the Standards and Operations Studio surface.
The severity mapping is set explicitly, because the platform never assumes one and at least one mapping is required on any screen that can deviate.
STATE-04 validation on the Studio surface carries special weight: the locale completeness check and the missing-severity-mapping check are publication blockers, not warnings.
Worker-facing content is held as per-locale authored variants inside one Workflow, never as parallel per-language versions.
Three prohibitions bind every Command Center screen absolutely: no gate override, no run pause or stop, no record or configuration edit, and no Job or run creation.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Absence of capability in the Hub services the Command Center calls

business_rules.statement: The Read-only Auditor has no access to the Client Command Center surface at all.
Each Command Center role lands on the view it works from, and the landing decides only the first screen.

Every one of the ten Command Center actions is a command against a Delivery Operations Hub record executed through the owning service and written to the Hub audit trail; there is no separate Command Center database.
Skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All and require individual Quality Manager resolution.
Nothing about pace is ever rendered to a worker in any module, any state, any release.
business_rules.enforcement_point: No pace field exists in the work package or the command channel

business_rules.statement: Captured media never touches the device gallery.
Nothing on the Frontline surface may imply that an offline device received or applied anything — the sync indicator never hides state and never implies a synchronisation that has not happened.
Exactly six destinations exist on the Frontline application; capture, coaching, deviation handling, handover, and sign-off are states of the Run Player, not separate destinations.
There is no on-device worker override of a qualification gate in either posture (strict or notify).
The player never advances past a step whose capture did not commit locally.
The Training Library is available only when connected, never required mid-run, and creates no production record.
Media is evicted from the device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check.
No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console; record-level content requires one of the three named access classes.
Mutating changes ride maker-checker, with ten named critical-class actions requiring root approval.
Six invariants render locked with an enforced badge and no off position for any account including the root.
business_rules.enforcement_point: No approval path, no configuration key

business_rules.statement: Operational tabs on a tenant are read-only by construction — no gate decision, lot release, deviation action, or assignment can be taken from the console.
Support reads only; no write capability exists inside a normal support session. A data repair goes through the compliance-emergency path, which requires the root and one Admin.
A persistent banner appears in the tenant's own interface naming the engineer and the start time, with an end-session control the tenant may exercise at any moment.

A decision taken against a stale approval-queue item is re-validated server-side before it applies; any request whose object changed underneath it is returned to its proposer rather than approved against a stale difference.
One producer per record type; where a second surface appears to write, it calls the producer's service.
The same service, the same rules — a seam is never a second implementation; it is a second caller.
Honesty at the boundary — every seam that crosses the device boundary must expose its true state, never a collapsed 'synced'.
The audit is part of the transaction; a seam cannot be 'best effort' on its audit leg.
Configurability never loosens: any seam carrying a configured value is bounded by the tenant-configuration registry, which rejects an out-of-bound value outright rather than accepting and logging it.
business_rules.applies_to: Every seam carrying a configured value

business_rules.statement: Where the Statement of Work does not name a single producer for a record type, stop and raise a Client Decision Required item rather than choosing; the seam is not built at V1.

A run cannot be started on a device unless the pinned package contains all screen content, specification limits, gate rules, severity mappings with the tenant action bundles, and the platform deviation-capture forms.
Absence of short-form coaching assets does not block run start, and the absence is displayed rather than hidden.
A Job cannot transition to `active` where the approver identity equals the creator identity.
A workflow cannot publish where any of the three approval stages is unsigned or where two stages carry the same identity.
A Severity 1 Hold always resolves to exactly one target, selected as Lot where a lot exists, else Unit where work is serialized, else Run.
No surface exposes an edit path on a published Workflow version, an Evidence object, or an audit entry.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Object-state check; no update endpoint exists

business_rules.statement: An orphaned capture is quarantined and visible in the sync-conflict review panel, never dropped and never counted in a summary.
An unclassified upstream dependency is treated as `Hard` until proven otherwise, because that is the conservative direction.
Every record type has exactly one cell reading `Allowed` as sole owner, or an explicitly stated split with the layer boundary named; no cell in the source-of-truth matrix is blank.
The worker-facing compliance-suspension message is exactly 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.'
business_rules.applies_to: Frontline Worker Application under compliance suspension

business_rules.statement: In-app notifications cannot be muted by any role, so no recipient loses every channel.
A notification is never the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension, or a device command.
No code path exists where a change lands and its audit row does not; no surface exposes an audit delete or edit path.
No seam's retry is unbounded; every retry state has an exhaustion transition.
No fallback silently discards or overwrites data, and no fallback presents stale data as current or failure as success.
No fallback depends indefinitely on one named person; escalation is always role-based with a stated fallback tier.
Never show an action as completed merely because the server created a command, and never use 'synced' as the only state.
The upward channel is never lossy; the queue is durable and resumable, survives a mid-sync drop, and resumes where it left off.
The downward channel is never immediate; there is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run.
Safety never rides the downward channel; anything that must act the instant it happens, most importantly the Severity 1 hold, is handled locally and never sent down a wire.
Sync is never a worker action; a manual sync control exists only as a convenience, never as a dependency.
`uploaded` never triggers device-side eviction; quarantined and rejected both retain the capture and neither deletes it.
The Frontline Worker Application never displays a state it cannot substantiate from its own knowledge.
No surface states that a command took effect on a device before that device acknowledged it; command application is idempotent and commands apply in the order they were pulled.
All nine capture-envelope elements are present on every accepted capture; a missing element causes quarantine.
Named-location provenance carries names only; no capture or operational event carries a geographic coordinate.
An operational event carrying a deterministic result is rejected, not accepted and ignored; an operational event can never place a hold, raise a deviation, or fail a gate.
Where a second-identity step-up applied, the authorising identity is captured against that specific authorisation, not against the session.
Every scheduled event produces a scheduled-run record for every intended occurrence, including occurrences that produced no output; a missed occurrence is reported as missed, never as empty.
Any additional qualifying operational signal must carry no deterministic result, be incapable of triggering a deviation, a hold, or a gate, and must not duplicate a capture.
A second override in the same area in the same shift escalates to the Quality Manager; clearance duration is uniform at tenant level, never per user.
Recertification requires the new expiry to postdate the old; back-dating the issue date is allowed with both certification date and entry date recorded.
No worker may attest their own qualification; qualifications are supervisor-entered with full audit.
No worker types a part number to satisfy a consumption reference; an inline-added part receives a platform-minted identifier and an unresolved part reference is flagged, never fabricated.
The Training Library never appears empty when the true cause is being offline; no training asset is present in an offline package.

Every Severity 1 deviation appears in the Anomaly Register as Critical with its containment record attached; a reclassification always carries a recorded reason and no anomaly closes without a closure note.
No tenant setting is writable except through the registry; an out-of-bound write fails and states the bound; no looser-than-floor value is ever stored, on any path.
A catalog change never re-bases an in-flight run; a Severity 1 action bundle can never be reduced below the floor by any distribution path.
No tile displays a healthy state on absent telemetry; pending counts reconcile exactly against arrivals.
A skew-flagged device never decides a conflict by its own timestamp; a tenant cannot set the skew threshold above the 60-minute ceiling.
A worker touching three runs in one shift meters one Worker-Shift; a substitution meters two; the ladder events at 80, 100 and 125 per cent plus burst entry always fire and cannot be disabled.
Every screen action in Chapter 25 maps to exactly one endpoint and one named server-side check chain of the six checks; no authority decision anywhere depends on a control being absent from a client.
Cross-tenant references are refused at check two before any role evaluation occurs.
No endpoint exists for any capability the Statement of Work places outside a surface, including gate override and run stop from an oversight surface.

Terminal safe state when a server-side check is missing or wrong: the endpoint is disabled at the gateway, degrading dependent screens to read-only — availability is deliberately sacrificed to authorisation.
Reversal of actions taken without authority is done through the platform's normal, audited paths — never by direct data edit.
Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class, or tag.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Role check on the lot-release endpoint

business_rules.statement: No claim of 100 per cent coverage is made while an open decision remains.

decisions.question: What is the target accessibility conformance standard and level for the platform's surfaces?
options: a recognised international standard at a stated level
a client-internal standard
no commitment
decisions.impact: Procurement risk for public-sector or large-enterprise tenants versus testing cost

decisions.question: May a granted qualification clearance be revoked before its duration elapses, and what happens to a run already resumed under it?
options: (a) add a revocation command as a sixth instance within the qualification-clearance class, applied at next sync, with the run re-parking at the next gate evaluation
(b) rely on suspension, which is disproportionate
(c) accept that clearances are irrevocable within their duration
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, raised new in Section 26.8.1
decisions.impact: A supervisor granting a clearance in error has no stated path to withdraw it

decisions.question: What validity period, if any, applies to each command class, and what happens to a command undelivered indefinitely?
options: (a) no expiry for any class, with supersession as the only replacement mechanism
(b) per-class expiry aligned to natural boundaries such as shift end for reassignment and clearance, and no expiry for suspension and lot release
(c) a single platform-wide expiry
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, raised new in Section 27.3
decisions.impact: A stale reassignment applied hours after shift end is actively wrong

decisions.question: Does a reconnecting device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
options: commands first (safety)
captures first (data integrity)
decisions.adopted_working_position: stop-class commands apply before the drain, every pending capture then uploads with nothing discarded, and the enabling-class commands apply after it
decisions.status: adopted working position, 2026-08-14, both source readings retained
decisions.impact: Determines whether a suspension lands before more work is created

decisions.question: Which list of seven capture types is the platform contract — the §1.7/§7.8.3 list or the §5.5.3 list?
options: §1.7 and §7.8.3: measurement, scan, photo, checklist, boolean, e-signature, free text
§5.5.3: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or quick-response scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, dropdown selection
decisions.adopted_working_position: the §5.5.3 set of seven capture types, dropdown selection included and checkbox confirmation carrying a multiplicity setting
decisions.impact: A Frontline player cannot render a type the contract does not name

decisions.question: Is the Site level mandatory as the required minimum hierarchy depth?
options: §2.1: open drafting recommendation
§4.3.1: 'The Site level is mandatory'
decisions.adopted_working_position: the Site level mandatory with a default Site auto-created at tenant provisioning
decisions.impact: Site drawn as required; first precondition satisfied at provisioning rather than onboarding

decisions.question: Is a Job anchored to one Area as a hard constraint, or to one parent node at the tenant's configured depth?
options: §2.1: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
§4.5.1: one Area per Job is a hard constraint
decisions.adopted_working_position: a Job anchored at the deepest parent node its tenant configured — one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
decisions.impact: Object relationship diagram draws one parent node per Job

decisions.question: How is soft suspension released — by explicit operator signal or automatically on a payment event?
options: §4.2.4: released by an explicit operator signal, not a payment event; no payment integration exists
§8.9.2 and Part IX: automatic on payment
decisions.adopted_working_position: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, with no payment event observed because there is no payment integration at V1
decisions.impact: Soft suspension exit path in the console

decisions.question: How is agent gating declared?
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field
decisions.status: adopted working position, 2026-08-14, both source readings retained in its card
decisions.impact: Governance gate queue behaviour on the Client Command Center

decisions.question: What is the content of the platform-seeded taxonomy catalogue at version 1?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the platform-seeded catalogue empty at version 1, with the sixteen starter names still owed by the client and never invented
decisions.impact: Studio content libraries seeded empty at V1

decisions.question: Does a trace viewer screen exist at version one on the Super Admin console?

backend tooling only, no console screen

decisions.question: What custody procedure covers the single root account when it is unavailable?

decisions.question: What is the device behaviour when local storage is exhausted?

decisions.question: What happens when a remote wipe is issued to a device that never returns, given a final synchronisation attempt is required before erasure?

decisions.question: How does library-edit pointer propagation interact with per-run package pinning for an in-flight run?

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Detection of any listed failure mode: delivery interruption; validation rejection; dependency unavailability; authority unavailable; storage exhaustion; clock untrustworthiness
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded safe retry or resume on the durable queue
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The pinned package's deterministic path, then the authored manual workflow, then role-based human escalation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled hold or safe stop with the state displayed honestly; data retained, hold in force where one was placed, no false success displayed, no unaudited change committed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection, queue drain, ordered command application, package re-pull; exit on dependency restoration plus successful reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A screen renders an action a role may not perform, or renders data outside the role's scope
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The server refuses the call and the client renders the permission-denied state with the reason and the route to request authority
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The server does not refuse, which is a security defect, not a usability defect
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The endpoint is disabled at the gateway and the dependent screen enters read-only until the check is corrected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fix the server-side check, not the client; replay the audit log for the affected endpoint over the exposure window and report any action taken without authority to the tenant

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A screen collapses two states into one, most commonly rendering STATE-12 as STATE-01
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The underlying service cannot distinguish the conditions, for example returning an empty list for both 'none exist' and 'query timed out'
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The screen renders STATE-12 with the text 'The platform could not confirm this list'
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The service is corrected to distinguish the conditions; no data reconciliation is needed because no data was written

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The review queue cannot load on the Delivery Operations Hub
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The screen renders STATE-12 naming the failed read and confirming that nothing was written
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The surface serves reads where it can and blocks every write; the floor is unaffected because device-side execution has no dependency on this surface being writable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Service restoration; late captures fold in flagged inside the record-finish window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The connection drops mid-authoring in the Standards and Operations Studio
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The panel preserves unsaved input locally in the browser session and renders STATE-12 naming what was not saved; nothing is submitted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The last saved draft stands and the published version is untouched, so the floor is unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The author reopens the draft; the version history shows no phantom version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The pushed-event channel drops, so the Command Center board stops receiving deviations
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The board falls back to its refresh cycle and labels every element with its age
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The board renders STATE-12 with all ten actions unavailable; the floor is unaffected since detection, classification, containment, and the Severity 1 hold are local to the device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Channel restoration, then replay of pushed events in server-receipt order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Frontline connectivity absent (the designed operating condition); then a local write fails; then device storage exhausts; then a remote wipe reaches a device that never returns
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Full local execution from the pinned package; on local write failure the player refuses to advance and asks for re-entry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Storage exhaustion behaviour deferred (DEC-STORE-001); never-returns wipe behaviour undefined (DEC-WIPE-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The encrypted local store retains every capture, media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, and the run either continues or holds — it never silently discards
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection; queue drain ordered by server receipt, commands applied in order, hold propagation to sibling devices, conflict review in the Command Center

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An approval cannot be recorded on the Super Admin console
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refusal, with the operator told the change has not been applied
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A queue backlog with the root unavailable, since exactly one root account exists and ten critical-class actions have no other approver
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing applies; the platform continues on its last approved configuration; tenants keep operating and the deterministic layer on every device is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Root action, or the custody procedure the client owes under DEC-ROOT-001; on restoration every pending request is re-validated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A server-side check is missing or wrong on an endpoint
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The defect reached production and actions were taken without authority
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The endpoint is disabled at the gateway, degrading dependent screens to read-only — availability is deliberately sacrificed to authorisation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fix and redeploy the server-side check; replay the audit log across the exposure window and reverse unauthorised actions through normal audited paths

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Envelope drift — an operational signal acquiring a deterministic result field
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Schema-level separation: the two envelopes are distinct types and the lighter one has no result field to populate
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A shared schema with optional fields
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform rejects an operational event carrying a result field, rather than accepting and ignoring it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Schema correction; review of every operational event that carried a result during the defect window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A capture stuck at `uploaded` without ever reaching `server received`
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: `uploaded` is never treated as success by the device; media eviction requires confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capture remains on the device in `queued` state with the worker's count and the Command Center pending count reflecting it, indefinitely
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A successful upload; device-to-server pending-count comparison

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An acknowledged-state gap: a device applies a command and the acknowledgement is lost
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device re-reports application state on its next sync, and the server treats a duplicate application as idempotent
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A command applied twice because idempotency was not implemented
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Command application is idempotent by design — applying a lot release twice releases once
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Acknowledgement on a later sync; created-versus-acknowledged comparison per device, which is the propagation-lag telemetry source

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scheduled event fires and is not recorded, indistinguishable from an event that did not fire
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The schedule-identifier and scheduled-run-identifier pair makes every intended occurrence enumerable whether or not it produced output
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A scheduled event with no scheduled-run record
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A schedule with no run record for an elapsed intended time is reported as missed, never as empty
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A catch-up run per the resolved DEC-SCHED band; comparison of intended occurrences against recorded runs per period
